messages:
nina: quick idea — lightweight contiguous relocator to reduce tiny-object scatter. runs opportunistically and cooperatively per-arena.

omar: high level? sounds like the hot-chunk packer convo but leaner.

nina: leaner: operate at object granularity with a relocation handle (RH) indirection to avoid heavy descriptor shuffles. RH is inserted only for candidate objects during low-signal windows.

tess: indirection on hot path is concerning. what's the perf trade?

nina: microbench shows ~1-2% P99 hit for a single extra load, but we win back by >10% fewer KV cache misses and fewer page splits for attention-kv cases.

omar: how to migrate without stopping inference?

nina: cooperative handshake:

1) relocator reserves dest and installs RH->MOVING with old_addr recorded
2) owner drains short in-flight ops (per-batch yield)
3) async copy on compaction stream (prefer same-device peer copy)
4) CAS backptr MOVING->READY with new addr + bump epoch
5) quick fenced window where lookups seeing MOVING fall back to old_addr
6) release old pages when epoch safe

tess: need eviction handshake — evictor must respect a relocation lease so source not reclaimed mid-copy.

omar: tenant fairness and DMA throttling?

nina: yes. compaction is tenant-aware, rate-limited by tenant quota. config knobs: enabled, tenant_rate_limit, global_bandwidth_limit, host_pinned_budget. infra-bot: please record defaults.

infra-bot: noted defaults — enabled=true, tenant_rate_limit=40MB/s, global_bandwidth_limit=800MB/s, host_pinned_budget=0.08*GPU_MEM.

tess: failure modes?

nina: CAS fail -> retry later; copy error -> mark RH ABORT and pin source; insufficient host-pinned -> decline and queue. Metrics to emit: bytes_moved, successes, aborts, avg_quiesce_ms, fragmentation_delta.

omar: tests: same-device copy, cross-device GPUDirect off, heavy-evict churn, CAS race injection. Add a short per-thread backptr cache to avoid repeated indirections — invalidate on epoch bump.

tess: sounds reasonable. draft a short RFC with sequence diagram and backptr layout (state, old_addr, new_addr, epoch). I'll review the telemetry bits.

nina: thanks — will post RFC in #eng-runtime tomorrow. :+1:
